title: Arrays, pointer arithmetic and T**
summary: p + 1 moves one element. Pointers to pointers. Reading const.

cards.title: Boxes in a row
cards.body: Array elements sit side by side. Look at the addresses: they go up by `sizeof(int)` each time.

cards.title: The code
cards.body: `p + 2` is scaled by the type: for `int*` it moves 2 × `sizeof(int)` bytes. For a `double*` it would move 2 × 8 bytes. And `p[i]` is literally defined as `*(p + i)`.

cards.question: What does this print?
cards.explain: p points at a[1]. p + 2 points at a[3], which is 40.

cards.title: Pointers to pointers
cards.body: `int**` is just a pointer whose target happens to be another pointer. Follow the arrows.

cards.title: Reading const without fear
cards.body:
Rule: `const` applies to the thing on its **left**. If nothing is on its left, it applies to the thing on its right.

- `const int* p` (same as `int const* p`): the **int** is const. You can't do `*p = 5`, but you can re-point p.
- `int* const p`: the **pointer** is const. You can do `*p = 5`, but not `p = &other`.
- `const int* const p`: neither can change.

Read right to left: `int* const p` is "p is a const pointer to int".

cards.question: Given `int* const p = &a;`, which line is an error?
cards.explain: The const is to the right of `*`, so the pointer itself is const. You may change the int (`*p = 9`) but not where p points.
